angle: Open-source ASR engines/approaches for VERBATIM transcripts that retain fillers (um/uh) with word-level timestamps and per-word confidence. Core finding confirmed: vanilla Whisper/Google deliberately drop disfluencies, so a verbatim-tuned engine OR a verbatim decode setting + a disfluency-aware step is mandatory to count fillers. The field splits into three tiers: (1) purpose-built verbatim+disfluency models (CrisperWhisper) that natively emit [UM]/[UH] with disfluency-robust timestamps; (2) Whisper-derivative timestampers (whisper-timestamped, WhisperX, stable-ts, faster-whisper) that give word timestamps+confidence but only keep fillers opportunistically unless coaxed (verbatim initial_prompt, detect_disfluencies, no-condition decode); (3) forced-alignment / non-Whisper engines (torchaudio wav2vec2 CTC, NeMo Forced Aligner, Vosk) that align an external verbatim transcript to audio for word timing+scores. Best practice for filler-counting: pair a verbatim transcript source with a forced aligner, or run a dedicated disfluency detector (amritkromana) on top. Two corrections to the prior list below.

repos.name: nyrahealth/CrisperWhisper
repos.whatItDoes: Purpose-built VERBATIM ASR. Fine-tuned Whisper large-v3 that transcribes every spoken word including fillers, stutters, false starts and pauses, emitting explicit [UM]/[UH] tokens. Uses an adjusted tokenizer + custom attention loss for timestamps that stay accurate AROUND disfluencies and pauses (the hardest case). This is the single best native fit for um/uh counting.
repos.libraries: Custom transformers fork (pip install git+https://github.com/nyrahealth/transformers.git@crisper_whisper); HF pipeline with return_timestamps='word'; PyTorch 2.x; Python 3.10; CUDA cuBLAS 11.x/cuDNN 8.x for GPU, CPU works but slow. Snippet: model=AutoModelForSpeechSeq2Seq.from_pretrained('nyrahealth/CrisperWhisper'); pipe=pipeline('automatic-speech-recognition', model=model, return_timestamps='word'); out=pipe('audio.wav'); for c in out['chunks']: c['text'], c['timestamp']=(start,end). Word probability not exposed natively (run a forced-align/score pass if confidence required).
repos.license: CC BY-NC 4.0 — NON-COMMERCIAL. FLAG: cannot be used in a commercial product. (Base Whisper is MIT, but the released fine-tuned weights carry the NC restriction.)
repos.techniques: Verbatim fine-tune + disfluency-aware tokenizer + custom attention loss for pause/disfluency-robust word timestamps. WER 6.66% avg across 8 datasets vs Whisper large-v3 7.7% (1.74% LibriSpeech-clean, 3.35% TED-LIUM).

repos.name: linto-ai/whisper-timestamped
repos.whatItDoes: Adds word-level timestamps AND per-word confidence to OpenAI Whisper via DTW on cross-attention weights (no extra model). Has an explicit detect_disfluencies=True mode that inserts [*] markers where the model swallowed a hesitation — the only Whisper timestamper with a built-in disfluency hook. Still inherits Whisper's tendency to drop fillers, so combine detect_disfluencies with a verbatim initial_prompt + condition_on_previous_text=False.

Snippet: import whisper_timestamped as whisper; m=whisper.load_model('large-v3', device='cuda'); r=whisper.transcribe(m, whisper.load_audio('a.wav'), detect_disfluencies=True, language='en'); for s in r['segments']: for w in s['words']: w['text'], w['start'], w['end'], w['confidence']. CPU or GPU (install torch+cpu for CPU-only).

repos.name: pytorch/audio (torchaudio) wav2vec2 forced alignment

The canonical way to get accurate word timing + scores for ANY transcript that already contains the fillers — you supply the verbatim text (e.g. transcribed by CrisperWhisper or hand-corrected) and it times every token including um/uh.

CPU or GPU.

repos.name: amritkromana/disfluency_detection_from_audio
repos.whatItDoes: Dedicated disfluency detector (not an ASR). Classifies five disfluency types — filled pauses (FP, i.e. um/uh), partial words (PW), repetitions (RP), revisions (RV), restarts (RS) — via language (Whisper+BERT), acoustic (WavLM), or multimodal (BLSTM fusion) modes. CORRECTION to prior note: the acoustic backbone is WavLM, not wav2vec2. Run as a post/parallel step over a verbatim transcript+audio to label and count fillers robustly, including ones ASR may have normalized.

repos.techniques: Whisper+BERT (text), WavLM (acoustic), BLSTM multimodal fusion; 5-class disfluency tagging at 20ms granularity; Switchboard training.

techniques: Verbatim decode settings on any Whisper engine: set condition_on_previous_text=False (stops the model 'cleaning up' across windows), supply a filler-laden initial_prompt ('Umm, uh, like, you know, I mean...') to prime verbatim style, and avoid suppress_tokens that strip hesitations. This is the cheapest way to push a standard Whisper toward keeping um/uh.

Two-stage verbatim+align pattern (most reliable for counting): Stage 1 produce a verbatim transcript that contains the fillers (CrisperWhisper, or human-corrected). Stage 2 force-align that exact text to audio with torchaudio wav2vec2 CTC or NeMo NFA to get accurate per-word start/end + averaged-probability confidence. Decouples recognition quality from timestamp quality.

Disfluency-marker hook: whisper-timestamped detect_disfluencies=True inserts [*] tokens where the model perceives a swallowed hesitation, giving you gap evidence even when the literal 'um' wasn't decoded.

Forced alignment = recognition + a known transcript. wav2vec2 CTC: log_softmax emissions -> trellis (max(prev+blank, trans+token_prob)) -> Viterbi backtrack -> merge identical tokens -> split on word-boundary token -> word spans; confidence = mean frame probability over the span. NeMo NFA does the same via CTC log-probs and also exports segment level.

Confidence sources differ per engine: whisper-timestamped word['confidence'] and faster-whisper word.probability come from aggregated token log-probabilities; WhisperX 'score' and torchaudio/NFA come from alignment frame probabilities; Vosk 'conf' from the Kaldi lattice. They are NOT directly comparable across engines — normalize before thresholding.

Filler-aware metrics on top of word output: filler_rate = filler_words / total_words * 100; WPM from word timestamps (sum words / total speaking-time minutes); inter-word silence/pause detection from gaps between word.end and next word.start (great for catching 'silent' hesitations the lexicon missed); type-token ratio (TTR) for vocabulary richness.

Real-time/embedded path: Vosk (streaming, SetWords(True), CPU-only) or NeMo streaming Parakeet for low-latency word timing+conf when you can't afford GPU batch inference; Whisper-family engines are batch/near-real-time at best.
metricsOrFormulas: filler_rate (%) = (count of filler tokens) / (total words) * 100
WPM = total_words / (total_speaking_seconds / 60); coaching ideal band commonly cited ~111-140 WPM
Type-Token Ratio (vocabulary richness) = unique_words / total_words
Pause/hesitation detection: gap = word[i+1].start - word[i].end; flag gap > threshold (e.g. 0.3-0.5s) as a silent hesitation even when no lexical filler present
Word confidence (Whisper-derivative) = exp(mean token log-prob over the word) -> whisper-timestamped word['confidence'] / faster-whisper word.probability
Forced-alignment confidence (wav2vec2 CTC / NFA) = (sum of per-frame probabilities over the token/word span) / (number of frames in span)
Frame->time conversion in wav2vec2 alignment: seconds = frame_index * (waveform_length / emission_length) / sample_rate
WER comparison (verbatim quality): CrisperWhisper 6.66% avg over 8 datasets vs Whisper large-v3 7.7% (LibriSpeech-clean 1.74%, TED-LIUM 3.35%)
recommendations: (a) COMMERCIAL + OFFLINE: faster-whisper (MIT, large-v3) as the recognizer with word_timestamps=True (gives word.start/.end/.probability), condition_on_previous_text=False, and a filler-laden initial_prompt to retain um/uh; then force-align the verbatim text with torchaudio wav2vec2 (use WAV2VEC2_ASR_BASE_960H, NOT the CC-BY-NC MMS_FA weights) or NeMo NFA for crisp word timing. Add amritkromana-style disfluency logic only after confirming/obtaining a license (currently unlicensed). This stack is fully permissive, runs offline on CPU or GPU, and avoids every NC trap.

(b) BEST ACCURACY (research / internal / non-commercial OK): CrisperWhisper — it is the only engine purpose-built to emit [UM]/[UH] with timestamps that stay accurate around disfluencies, and it beats Whisper large-v3 on WER. Use it to produce the verbatim transcript, then force-align with torchaudio/NFA if you need per-word confidence (CrisperWhisper does not expose word probability natively). HARD CONSTRAINT: CC BY-NC 4.0 means non-commercial only — never ship it in a paid product.

Do NOT rely on vanilla Whisper, WhisperX, or Google STT alone to count fillers: they normalize away um/uh by design and the wav2vec2 aligner can skip the few that survive. A verbatim transcript source is mandatory before any counting.

License flags to enforce: CrisperWhisper = CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial); whisper-timestamped = AGPL-3.0 (copyleft, risky for closed SaaS); amritkromana/disfluency_detection_from_audio = NO license file (all-rights-reserved, research-only until clarified); torchaudio MMS_FA alignment weights = CC-BY-NC (pick the LibriSpeech wav2vec2 model for commercial use). Safe-commercial cores: faster-whisper (MIT), WhisperX (BSD-2), stable-ts (MIT, but unmaintained), Vosk (Apache-2.0), NeMo framework (Apache-2.0, verify each checkpoint card).

If you need real-time / on-device filler feedback (e.g. live presentation coaching): use Vosk (Apache-2.0, CPU, streaming, SetWords(True) gives word+conf+timestamps) or a streaming NeMo Parakeet model, accepting lower verbatim accuracy than the Whisper-class batch pipeline.

Robust counting architecture overall: verbatim ASR (CrisperWhisper or faster-whisper+verbatim prompt) -> forced alignment (torchaudio CTC / NeMo NFA) for word timing+confidence -> a disfluency/pause pass (whisper-timestamped detect_disfluencies marker, gap-based silent-hesitation detection, or a licensed disfluency classifier) -> metrics (filler_rate, WPM, TTR, pause stats).

angle: Filler-word AND broad-disfluency detection across two modalities. Audio-model approaches: verbatim ASR, wav2vec2 and neural semi-CRF acoustic classifiers, and stuttering-event models. Text-plus-timestamp heuristics: sequence labeling, span and parse-based detectors, and gap-and-repeat rules. The non-obvious through-line is that ordinary ASR such as Whisper and Google is trained to DROP fillers, so counting them requires either a verbatim ASR engine, an acoustic event detector, or operating on already-disfluent verbatim text. Beyond fillers, the literature uses a standard taxonomy worth scoring separately: filled pauses (um, uh, er); discourse markers and parentheticals (like, you know, I mean, so, basically, well); repetitions (word, phrase, sound, part-word); false starts and restarts; revisions and self-corrections; partial words; prolongations; and blocks. The strongest reusable assets are the pariajm awesome-disfluency-detection hub plus its MIT-licensed parser, the gzhu06 PodcastFillers and semi-CRF audio family, and Apple SEP-28k for stuttering-style events. Consumer tools (Voquill, daily-demos) show the verbatim-ASR-then-lexicon pattern in production.

repos.name: itsmevictor/clean-transcribe
repos.whatItDoes: CLI that transcribes YouTube or local media then LLM-cleans transcripts, removing fillers, fixing grammar, multi-provider across Gemini, ChatGPT, and Claude. An easy baseline for LLM-based disfluency removal to diff against rule-based counts.

techniques: VERBATIM-ASR-FIRST, mandatory for text-side counting. Whisper, Google, and most ASR delete fillers, so use a verbatim engine before any lexicon match. Options: CrisperWhisper for verbatim plus accurate word timestamps, whisper-timestamped for forced-alignment timestamps on standard Whisper, Deepgram Nova with filler_words true, faster-whisper with a verbatim prompt as in dougcalobrisi/erm, or wav2vec2 CTC which transcribes more literally than seq2seq Whisper.

TRANSCRIPTION-FREE AUDIO EVENT DETECTION, skip ASR entirely and classify acoustic frames or segments directly. gzhu06/Filler-semi-CRF uses a neural semi-CRF over wav2vec or log-mel to localize filler events with timestamps; amritkromana uses wav2vec2 embeddings into CNN or Transformer per disfluency type. Best for prolongations, blocks, and sound repetitions that have no clean text token.

SEQUENCE LABELING ON VERBATIM TEXT, token tagging. Tag each token as fluent, reparandum, interregnum, or repair in BIO style. BiLSTM-CRF or BERT token classification trained on Switchboard. Captures repetitions, corrections, false starts, and restarts at token granularity, as in vickyzayats and deep_disfluency.

SPAN OR PARSE-BASED DETECTION. Predict disfluent spans or EDITED constituency nodes rather than isolated tokens, better for multi-word false starts and revisions. See pariajm joint parser, MIT, and Sreyan88 span classification.
AUTO-CORRELATION ROUGH-COPY MODELING. Learn that a token resembles a recent token to catch repetitions and repairs without hand rules, as in deep-disfluency-detector.

PROSODY-AUGMENTED DETECTION. Add pause duration, word duration, and pitch F0 features to the text model; the gap-before-word and lengthening cues disambiguate filled pauses, prolongations, and repair boundaries. See trangham283/prosody_nlp and PodcastFillers VAD.

STUTTERING-EVENT MULTI-LABEL CLASSIFICATION. wav2vec2 plus a classification head over 3-second windows for blocks, prolongations, sound-rep, word-rep, and interjection. See SEP-28k and SEP-28k-Extended. A clip can carry multiple labels.

LLM POST-CLEANUP AS A DETECTOR. Prompt an LLM to remove fillers, false starts, and revisions, then diff against the verbatim transcript; the removed tokens are the detected disfluencies. Catches messy false starts lexicons miss, as in voquill and clean-transcribe, but is non-deterministic, so use for removal and UX, not for exact counts.
REAL-TIME FEEDBACK LOOP. Stream an incremental tagger or live classifier and surface filler events live. See clp-research incremental tagger and obkaul/AhemPreventor haptic.

DATA AUGMENTATION FOR LOW LABELS. Switchboard is only about 6 percent disfluent; synthesize repetitions, restarts, and repairs with GT-SALT, or self-train on unlabeled verbatim transcripts with scir-zywang, to train a custom detector.
metricsOrFormulas: Filler rate equals filler_count divided by total_words times 100, per the SharathKumar787 rubric. Also report fillers per minute equals filler_count divided by duration_minutes, more stable across speech length.
Disfluency rate equals disfluent_tokens divided by total_tokens. Switchboard baseline is about 6 percent disfluent, a useful normal-speech reference floor.
WPM speech rate equals words divided by duration_minutes. Rubric ideal band is about 111 to 140; slower can co-occur with more filled pauses.
Type-Token Ratio TTR equals unique_words divided by total_words for vocabulary richness. Confound: TTR drops with transcript length, so prefer MATTR or moving-average TTR over fixed windows.
Detector quality metric: EDITED-word F1, precision and recall on reparandum tokens, the standard Switchboard disfluency metric. The pariajm joint parser reports about 90.9.

Audio event metric: per-class and macro-F1 over labels such as uh, um, you-know, like, and repetition, the PodcastFillers coarse 5-class versus granular 6-class, plus event-level F1 with onset tolerance or IoU for semi-CRF localization. SEP-28k 5-class macro-F1 ranges about 0.28 to 0.50-plus.

GAP-BEFORE-WORD heuristic, needs word timestamps: flag a token as a candidate filled pause or hesitation if the inter-word gap immediately preceding it exceeds a threshold such as 0.2 to 0.3 seconds, and or if the token itself is a lexicon filler. Pause plus lexicon together cuts false positives versus lexicon alone.

REPEATED-TOKEN heuristic: flag immediate repetition when token at i lowercased equals token at i minus 1 (word repetition), or when an n-gram of length 2 to 4 repeats consecutively (phrase repetition such as I know I know). Collapse to detect stutter-style word repetition without acoustics.

PARTIAL-WORD or fragment heuristic: a token ending in a hyphen, or a non-dictionary prefix of the following token such as wou- then would, or oper- then operation, signals a false start or partial word.

PROLONGATION heuristic: in verbatim ASR output, a token with three-plus repeated characters such as whooo or sooo, or better an acoustic token whose duration is a large outlier versus that phone mean duration.

DISCOURSE-MARKER CONTEXT rules to reduce over-counting of legit content words: count like as filler only when NOT preceded by a copula or comparison such as is like, looks like, feels like, and NOT followed by a noun phrase it compares; count so as filler mainly utterance-initial; count well as filler utterance-initial; require know to be preceded by you for the you-know marker; treat right and okay as fillers mainly when tag-final.

REVISION or CORRECTION heuristic: detect reparandum-repair pairs where a span is restarted with overlapping head words separated by an edit term, such as to Sydney no to Melbourne; edit terms include no, sorry, I mean, rather, well acting as interregnum between reparandum and repair.
recommendations: Two-track architecture. Track A for counts and metrics: verbatim ASR with word timestamps such as CrisperWhisper or whisper-timestamped or Deepgram filler_words true, then a lexicon plus rule pass for fillers, discourse markers, repetitions, and partial words, emitting per-type counts, rate, and WPM. Track B for hard acoustic classes: a transcription-free audio model such as gzhu06/Filler-semi-CRF for fillers and a SEP-28k-trained wav2vec2 for prolongations, blocks, and sound-reps. Fuse on the timeline by timestamp.

Do not count fillers off plain Whisper or Google output; they strip um, uh, and like by design. Validate by transcribing a known clip with and without the verbatim engine and confirming the fillers reappear; treat this as a regression test.

Adopt the PodcastFillers plus SEP-28k label taxonomy as your schema: uh, um, you-know, like, word-rep, sound-rep, prolongation, block, false-start or revision, partial-word, interjection. It is the de-facto standard, gives ready-made training and eval data, and makes metrics comparable.

Make like, so, well, and right context-sensitive, not raw substring matches. Apply the discourse-marker context rules using POS, position, and collocation, or you will massively over-count legitimate uses such as it looks like or so that I could.

Combine pause plus lexicon for filled pauses: a lexicon hit that is also preceded by an above-threshold inter-word gap is a high-confidence filler; lexicon-only hits are lower confidence. This uses the word timestamps you already get from the verbatim engine.

For the strongest text-side detector with a clean license, start from pariajm/joint-disfluency-detector-and-parser, MIT, BERT, about 90.9 EDITED-F1, for repetitions, false starts, and revisions, then layer the finite filler and discourse-marker lexicon on top for the trivial classes it intentionally ignores.

If labeled data is the blocker, since Switchboard is only about 6 percent disfluent, augment with GT-SALT disfluency generation or self-train with scir-zywang on your own verbatim transcripts before fine-tuning.

Check each academic repo LICENSE file before any commercial use. Most are MIT such as the pariajm parser, but several list none; SEP-28k labels are CC-BY-NC-4.0 and PodcastFillers data is non-commercial research only. CrisperWhisper is CC BY-NC 4.0, non-commercial. Keep the audio datasets out of any shipped product and treat the verbatim engine license as the gating constraint.

Use the LLM-cleanup path such as voquill or clean-transcribe only for user-facing transcript polishing or to mine false-start examples, never as the counter of record, since it is non-deterministic and will silently rewrite content.

angle: Complete multimodal public-speaking / presentation / interview COACHING systems on GitHub — full feature sets, architectures, libraries, scoring rubrics, and UI approaches — mined for a MAXIMAL grading-system feature list. Emphasis on the most complete, verifiable open-source systems (academic multimodal feedback platforms + production real-time coach frameworks + LLM mock-interview platforms), beyond the filler-word/verbatim-ASR detectors already cataloged.

repos.name: xaoch/OpenOPAF
repos.whatItDoes: The single most complete open-source multimodal Oral Presentation Automated Feedback (OPAF) system (NYU, Xavier Ochoa, Journal of Learning Analytics 2024). Scores SIX named presentation skills, each with its own swappable 'scorer' module containing adjustable, culture-tunable thresholds: (1) Looking at the audience / eye contact, (2) Maintaining open posture, (3) Using gestures, (4) Maintaining adequate speech cadence (articulation rate), (5) Avoiding filled pauses, (6) Visual-aid quality split into avoiding too much text (TLen) + visible font size (FSize). Also captures speech volume. Web UI: login, start a session (set duration, optionally upload slides), then a reviewable post-session report + a progress dashboard across past sessions. Companion 3D-printed hardware kit (Jetson Nano) documented in /hardware.
repos.libraries: MediaPipe Holistic (3D body/face/hand landmarks → posture + Gaze/GazeDirection extractor GGDE); Parselmouth (Python PRAAT) with De Jong's scripts for volume, Articulation Rate (counts syllabic nuclei over rolling 5-second windows, converts to WPM assuming 1.66 syllables/word), and Filled Pauses (detects prolonged syllables with minimal spectral contrast); python-pptx + OCR for slide text length & font size; Flask backend; SQLite DB (create_database.py); JS/HTML/CSS frontend served at :5000. Modular pipeline: frame/audio capture → feature extractors → per-skill scorers → feedback generator.
repos.license: GPL-3.0 (paper states GPLv3 for code + 3D models; verify LICENSE file in repo)
repos.techniques: Per-skill scorer modules with externalized thresholds (e.g. eye contact 'mastered' = gaze on audience >=85% of time); rolling 5-second windowed audio analysis; syllable-nuclei articulation-rate estimation (1.66 syll/word); spectral-contrast filled-pause detection; statistical-mode aggregation of frames into reviewable segments; slide-text-density + font-size scoring; tunable-by-culture rubric design; real-time + post-hoc report duality.

repos.name: GetStream/Vision-Agents
repos.whatItDoes: Production-grade open framework for real-time voice+vision agents; the backbone of freeCodeCamp's 'Real-Time Public Speaking & Presentation Coach' (~50 lines of main.py). The coach build measures 7 dimensions: filler words (um/uh/like/you know), speaking pace (too fast/slow), vocal variety (monotone), clarity, posture (shoulders/back/chin), hand gestures, and eye contact. Agent runs autonomously — only speaks feedback after 3-5s of detected silence; replies are 1-2 sentences, positive-first, one actionable tip. Pluggable frame-by-frame processor pipeline (here ~6 fps) feeds a realtime speech-to-speech model.
repos.libraries: Stream Video (WebRTC edge transport, sub-30ms routing); Ultralytics YOLO11 pose (yolo11n-pose.pt, 17 keypoints) for posture/gesture; OpenAI Realtime API for low-latency speech-to-speech; integrations also include Gemini Live, AWS Nova Sonic, Qwen/Inworld realtime; STT (Deepgram, AssemblyAI, Fast-Whisper, Wizper, Voxtral); TTS (ElevenLabs, Cartesia, Kokoro, Polly); vision (Roboflow, Moondream, NVIDIA Cosmos); built-in Turn Detection + VAD.
repos.techniques: Silence-gated feedback (only coach during pauses, not mid-sentence); turn detection + VAD; pluggable pre/post-LLM frame processors; realtime multimodal fusion of pose keypoints + speech-to-speech; brevity-constrained coaching prompt (positive-first, 1 tip); fps-throttled vision sampling to control latency/cost.

repos.name: isaactony/AI-Interview-Coach

repos.techniques: Local-only pose inference (privacy posture); real-time keypoint overlay as the feedback channel; minimal-dependency single-loop architecture — good reference for the cheapest possible posture/gesture grader.

repos.whatItDoes: Not a coach itself but the de-facto face-behavior feature engine used by nearly every academic presentation-competence system. repos.license: Academic/research license (free for non-commercial academic use; NOT permissive — commercial use requires separate licensing)

repos.name: Sumer/ahcounter-style + CMU-MultimodalSDK reference (Estimating Presentation Competence, arXiv 2105.02636)
repos.whatItDoes: Reference taxonomy (Sümer et al.) for what a MAXIMAL grader can measure: fuses three nonverbal channels — speech, face (head pose + gaze + AUs), and body pose — over 251 student presentation videos to predict human rubric competence ratings. Establishes which channel fusions score best and the exact feature families to extract.
repos.libraries: OpenFace 2.0 (landmarks/head-pose/gaze/AUs), OpenPose (2D body joints: neck/shoulders/arms/wrists/elbows/hips), audio prosody (f0 mean/SD/max, speaking rate), classical models (SVR, Random Forest, GLM); time-aggregated statistics + histograms of feature co-occurrence.
repos.license: Paper (code availability varies); cite as design source
repos.techniques: Feature families to copy: f0 (pitch) mean/std/max, speaking rate, audio intensity; head-pose & gaze histograms; AU co-occurrence; body-joint displacement; lexical features (first-person pronoun count). Fusion of speech+face+body beats any single channel — directly informs a multimodal grading rubric.

techniques: VERBATIM ASR IS NON-NEGOTIABLE (correcting/confirming prior insight): standard Whisper/Google normalize away disfluencies, so fillers must come from a verbatim engine (CrisperWhisper, whisper-timestamped) OR an acoustic detector. OpenOPAF sidesteps ASR entirely for fillers — it detects filled pauses acoustically as prolonged syllables with minimal spectral contrast (Parselmouth/PRAAT), which is robust to ASR filler-stripping. Offer BOTH paths.

Per-skill scorer modules with externalized, tunable thresholds (OpenOPAF): each metric is its own module + threshold constant so rubrics can be re-tuned per culture/level without touching extraction. This is the cleanest grading architecture to copy.

Rolling fixed-window analysis (OpenOPAF uses 5-second windows) so every metric becomes a time series — enables a timeline view, trend detection (e.g. pace creeping up), and per-segment color coding rather than one summary number.
Articulation rate without ASR: count syllabic nuclei over a window and convert to WPM via ~1.66 syllables/word (De Jong & Wempe). Lets you score pace even when transcription is unavailable or noisy.

Multichannel fusion beats any single channel (Sümer et al.): combine speech + face + body. Best accuracy/regression came from fusion, not audio-only or pose-only — a maximal grader should fuse, then attribute the final score back to channels.

Eye-contact-with-audience % via gaze classification: random-forest GOOD/BAD per frame (RAP system) using eye/nose/ear keypoint angles+distances, or gaze vector from OpenFace/MediaPipe; 'mastered' threshold ~85% gaze-on-audience (OpenOPAF default).
Silence-gated coaching (Vision Agents): only deliver real-time feedback during detected pauses (3-5s silence) so you never talk over the speaker — pair VAD + turn detection.

Embodied/ambient real-time nudge vs. screen report (Prezence): real-time correction can be a non-textual signal (robot gesture, LED, haptic) measured against a configurable 'ideal delivery model'; pair with an end-of-session statistics report.
Two-tier feedback timing: live nudges during the run + a reviewable post-session report and a cross-session progress dashboard (OpenOPAF, adrianhajdin). Almost every complete system does both.

LLM-as-judge for content/answer quality (Interviewer, ai_mock_interviews): an LLM generates a category-scored rubric (strengths, gaps, actionable tips, final assessment) over the transcript — the content half that pairs with delivery metrics.

Persona/difficulty parameterization (mock-interviews-with-ai): configurable interviewer tone (Friendly→Challenging) and question-type taxonomy (Technical/Behavioral/Situational/Culture-Fit) double as a coverage rubric.
Slide/visual-aid grading (OpenOPAF): score text density (too much text) and font-size visibility via python-pptx + OCR — a presentation grader should grade the slides, not just the speaker.
Facial Action Units → expressiveness/affect (OpenFace): AU intensity time series detects smiling, brow tension (nervousness), and flat affect (under-expressive).
metricsOrFormulas: Eye contact mastery (OpenOPAF default): gaze directed at audience >= 85% of total time = mastered (threshold is meant to be tuned per culture/objective).
Articulation rate (OpenOPAF/De Jong): WPM = (syllabic nuclei counted over 5s window) * (60/5) / 1.66 syllables-per-word; analyze on rolling 5-second windows.
Pace target (from prior SharathKumar787 ref, keep): ideal WPM band ~111-140; flag <~110 (too slow/monotone) and >~150-160 (rushed).

Filler rate (SharathKumar787, confirmed): filler_rate = (filler_count / total_words) * 100. Filler list: um, uh, like, you know, so, actually, basically, right, i mean, well, kinda, sort of, okay, hmm, ah.
Acoustic filled-pause detection (OpenOPAF, no ASR needed): flag prolonged syllables with minimal spectral contrast within each 5s window.
Vocabulary richness: Type-Token Ratio (TTR) = unique_words / total_words (SpeakEZ/SharathKumar787); supplement with mean word complexity and common-word ratio (SpeakEZ).
Prosody features (Sümer et al.): fundamental frequency f0 mean, f0 standard deviation (monotone = low SD), f0 max, speaking rate, audio intensity (volume). Low f0-SD = monotone flag.
Volume: measured per 5s window in dB-equivalent (OpenOPAF, robust to typical classroom noise); score against a target loudness band, flag too-quiet/too-loud.

Pose/posture: 17 keypoints (YOLO11 pose) or OpenPose joints (neck/shoulders/arms/wrists/elbows/hips); derive shoulder symmetry, chin/head tilt, body-joint displacement variance (sway/fidget vs. stillness).
Gaze classification (RAP): per-frame GOOD/BAD via random forest over angles + normalized distances between facial keypoints (eyes, nose, ears).
Facial Action Units (OpenFace): per-frame AU occurrence + intensity → smile rate, brow-furrow (tension), and expressiveness range.
Slide quality (OpenOPAF): text-length per slide (TLen, lower=better) and font size (FSize, must exceed visibility threshold) via python-pptx + OCR.
Sentiment / keyword / named-entity coverage on the transcript (JermaineV/AI_Coach) for content scoring; pair with LLM rubric scores (Interviewer/ai_mock_interviews).
Frame sampling: ~6 fps was sufficient for real-time pose/gesture coaching (Vision Agents) — a cost/latency lever.
recommendations: Anchor the architecture on xaoch/OpenOPAF — it is the most complete verifiable open-source presentation grader (GPL-3.0): six tunable per-skill scorer modules, rolling 5s windows, acoustic filler detection, slide grading, web report + progress dashboard. Note GPL-3.0 is copyleft — if your product is closed-source, treat OpenOPAF as a design/reference, not a code import.

Build delivery-metric extraction as independent, threshold-externalized scorer modules (one per skill) so the rubric is re-tunable per audience/culture without touching the extractors. This is OpenOPAF's key reusable pattern.

Use TWO filler paths in parallel: (a) verbatim ASR (CrisperWhisper — flag its CC BY-NC-4.0 non-commercial license — or whisper-timestamped, MIT/permissive) for word-level filler timestamps; (b) OpenOPAF-style acoustic filled-pause detection via Parselmouth/PRAAT, which works even when ASR strips fillers and needs no transcript. Reconcile the two for a robust count.

Adopt a multimodal fusion grader (Sümer et al. proves fusion beats any single channel): speech prosody (f0 mean/SD/max, rate, intensity) + face (gaze %, head-pose stability, AU expressiveness) + body pose (posture, sway/gesture). Then attribute the composite score back to each channel for actionable feedback.

Pick the pose/face stack by license: YOLO11 pose (Ultralytics, AGPL-3.0 — copyleft, commercial license available) or MediaPipe (Apache-2.0, friendliest) for body/gesture; for gaze + facial Action Units, OpenFace is the richest but its license is academic/non-commercial — flag this trap and consider MediaPipe FaceLandmarker (Apache-2.0) blendshapes as a permissive substitute.

Implement silence-gated real-time feedback (Vision Agents): VAD + turn detection so the coach only speaks during 3-5s pauses, with 1-2 sentence positive-first tips — then a full post-session report + cross-session progress dashboard. Live + retrospective is what every complete system ships.

For the content/answer-quality half (interview mode), reuse the LLM-as-judge rubric pattern from IliaLarchenko/Interviewer (Apache-2.0) and adrianhajdin/ai_mock_interviews: per-category scores + strengths + gaps + final assessment over the transcript; parameterize interviewer persona and question-type taxonomy.
Don't skip slide grading for presentation mode (OpenOPAF): score text density and font-size visibility via python-pptx + OCR — a maximal grader grades the visual aids, not only the speaker.

Frameworks worth importing wholesale: GetStream/Vision-Agents (Apache-2.0) gives you WebRTC transport + turn detection + VAD + pluggable STT/TTS/vision processors out of the box, turning the coach into ~50 lines. Strong if you want production realtime fast.

Verify each repo's LICENSE file directly before importing — several tutorial repos (darrylschaefer, adrianhajdin, JermaineV, Prezence) had no confirmed license in metadata, and OpenFace + YOLO carry restrictive/copyleft terms that materially affect a commercial grading product.

angle: Concrete SCORING rubrics and exact metric formulas with threshold/ideal bands for speech & oral-presentation grading — WPM, filler rate, pause/articulation analysis, lexical diversity (TTR/MATTR/MTLD), lexical density, spoken-text readability/grade level, and grammar-error rate. Emphasis on defensible numbers traceable to repos OR peer-reviewed papers, and on the construct-driven research standard (ETS SpeechRater / utterance-fluency literature) that the already-found hobbyist tools approximate. KEY CONFIRMED INSIGHT preserved: standard ASR (Whisper, Google STT) deliberately removes disfluencies, so a verbatim engine (CrisperWhisper, whisper-timestamped, or a Praat/parselmouth acoustic path that needs no transcript) is mandatory for filler/pause counts. Two correctness notes on the already-found set: (1) WPM 'ideal' is context- and source-dependent — the 111-140 band in AI-Transcript-Scoring-Tool is one tool's choice; the broader evidence-backed comfortable range is ~130-160 WPM (Toastmasters 120-160; comprehension optimum ~150-160 per Univ. of Missouri-cited work). (2) Plain TTR is length-confounded and should NOT be used as an absolute richness score across responses of different lengths — use MATTR (50-word window) or MTLD instead; TTR is only safe at fixed/standardized length.

repos.name: Shahabks/my-voice-analysis
repos.whatItDoes: Praat/parselmouth voice analyzer that needs NO transcript — segments syllable nuclei and silences directly from audio. Exposes named functions: myspsyl (syllable count), mysppaus (pause count), myspsr (speech rate, syll/sec over total time), myspatc (articulation rate, syll/sec over phonation time only), myspst (speaking duration excl. pauses), myspod (total duration), myspbala (balance = speaking_duration/original_duration = phonation-time ratio), and f0 mean/sd/median/min/max/q25/q75. This is the cleanest open implementation of the speech-rate-vs-articulation-rate distinction.
repos.libraries: Praat (myspsolution.praat), parselmouth, numpy; WAV 44kHz/16-bit
repos.techniques: de Jong & Wempe syllable-nuclei detection; speech rate vs articulation rate vs phonation-time ratio (balance)

repos.name: Shahabks/myprosody
repos.whatItDoes: Sibling of my-voice-analysis adding scoring: avg syllable-pause duration, long pauses, articulation rate, words-per-minute, filler words, voiced-syllables/pause ratio, F0 stats, plus a TOEFL-scale score, Shannon index, intonation index, pronunciation posterior, CEFR level, and prosody-vs-native comparison. Cites Klaus Zechner (ETS SpeechRater) as the research basis.
repos.libraries: Praat, parselmouth, pickled ML models; WAV 48kHz
repos.techniques: construct-driven prosody scoring; TOEFL/CEFR mapping; intonation & Shannon indices

repos.name: Shahabks/Speechat

repos.name: de Jong & Wempe Praat syllable-nuclei script
repos.whatItDoes: Canonical Praat script that detects syllable nuclei and silences to compute speech rate, articulation rate, and pause counts WITHOUT a transcript. The acoustic source-of-truth underneath my-voice-analysis/myprosody; standard in L2-fluency research.
repos.libraries: Praat
repos.techniques: automatic syllable-nucleus & silent-pause detection; utterance-fluency measures

techniques: Verbatim-ASR-first pipeline (non-negotiable): Whisper/Google STT strip fillers and disfluencies by design, so route audio through a verbatim engine (nyrahealth/CrisperWhisper, linto-ai/whisper-timestamped) OR a transcript-free acoustic path (de Jong-Wempe Praat / parselmouth via my-voice-analysis) before counting fillers, repetitions, or pauses.

Two timing measures, kept separate (the single most-confused pair): SPEECH RATE = total syllables / total time INCLUDING pauses; ARTICULATION RATE = total syllables / phonation time EXCLUDING all silent+filled pauses. Report both — a fast articulation rate with low speech rate signals excessive pausing, not fast talking.
Phonation-time ratio (a.k.a. 'balance' in my-voice-analysis) = speaking time / total time. A compact single-number fluency proxy; low values = halting/over-paused delivery.

Silent-pause detection threshold: count a silence as a pause only if it exceeds ~250 ms (research convention is 250-300 ms; ETS SpeechRater 'longpfreq' counts silences > 0.5 s as long pauses). Report pause count, mean pause length, and long-pause frequency separately.

Length-robust lexical diversity: prefer MATTR (mean TTR over a sliding 50-word window) or MTLD (mean run length before TTR drops below 0.72) over raw TTR; HD-D/vocd-D for medium texts. Raw TTR only when sample length is fixed/standardized.

Lexical density via POS tagging: tag the transcript, then density = content words (noun/verb/adj/adverb) / total tokens * 100 (Ure) — spoken language characteristically sits BELOW ~40%, written above; do not penalize a speaker for sub-40% density, it is normal for speech.

Spoken-text readability/grade level: apply Flesch-Kincaid Grade / Flesch Reading Ease to the transcript using syllable counts, but treat absolute grade level cautiously — readability formulas were built for written prose; use relative change as the signal.

Grammar-error rate: run a GEC corrector to get edits, classify with ERRANT, then normalize as errors per 100 words = (edit_count / total_words) * 100; report by error type for actionable feedback. CEFR-style: grammatical-error-rate correlated ~0.73 with human grammar-accuracy scores in CEFR-J work.

Construct-driven composite (ETS SpeechRater pattern): score independent constructs — delivery/fluency, pronunciation, prosody/rhythm, vocabulary, grammar, content — then weight into a final band, rather than one opaque number. SpeechRater v5 uses ~24 features across these constructs.
Acoustic filler detection as a complement: for real-time coaching where no verbatim transcript exists, an acoustic detector (AhemPreventor, um_detector) flags 'um/uh' from audio features directly.
metricsOrFormulas: WPM (speech rate, words) = (word_count / duration_seconds) * 60. Ideal/comfortable band ~130-160 WPM (Toastmasters 120-160; comprehension optimum ~150-160 WPM, Univ. of Missouri-cited; ~140 WPM perceived most credible). Slow <120, fast >170-200. [Note: AI-Transcript-Scoring-Tool uses 111-140 as its 'ideal' — narrower and tool-specific.]
Speech rate (syllables) = total_syllables / total_time_incl_pauses (syll/sec). Fluent-adult normal ~4-5 syll/sec (~162-230 syll/min).
Articulation rate = total_syllables / phonation_time_excl_pauses (syll/sec). Fluent-adult normal ~4.0-5.9 syll/sec; children ~2.9-4.2; adultlike by ~age 10.
Phonation-time ratio (balance) = speaking_time / total_time. (my-voice-analysis myspbala = speaking_duration / original_duration.)
Speech-to-pause ratio = total_speech_time / total_silence_time.

Filler rate (%) = (filler_count / total_words) * 100. Normal spontaneous-speech filled-pause (um/uh) baseline ~1.6-3.0 per 100 words (Bortfeld et al. 2001: ~2.6; Shriberg 1994: 1.6-2.2; men ~3.04 vs women ~2.07); total disfluencies ~6 per 100 words. So filler RATE >~6/100 is elevated, >~10/100 distracting. Default filler list: um, uh, like, you know, so, actually, basically, right, i mean, well, kinda, sort of, okay, hmm, ah.
Disfluencies-per-second (SpeechRater 'dpsec') = count(um/eer/repairs) / duration_sec; Long-pause frequency (SpeechRater 'longpfreq') = count(silences > 0.5 s).
Silent-pause threshold: silence counts as a pause if duration > ~250 ms (range used in literature 250-300 ms).
Type-Token Ratio (TTR) = unique_words / total_words (0-1; length-confounded — falls as length grows; use only at fixed length).
MATTR = mean of TTR computed over every sliding window of W tokens (W=50 standard); stable across lengths.

MTLD = mean number of tokens needed for sequential TTR to fall to the 0.72 factor threshold (computed forward and backward, averaged); length-independent. HD-D/vocd-D = probabilistic TTR estimate via hypergeometric sampling.
Lexical density (Ure) = (content_word_tokens / total_tokens) * 100. Halliday variant = content_words / number_of_clauses. Spoken language typically <40%, written >40%.
Flesch Reading Ease = 206.835 - 1.015*(words/sentences) - 84.6*(syllables/words). 0-100; higher = easier (60-70 ~ plain English).
Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level = 0.39*(words/sentences) + 11.8*(syllables/words) - 15.59 → US grade.

Grammar-error rate = (grammatical_edit_count / total_words) * 100 (errors per 100 words), edits typed via ERRANT; GEC systems scored with M2/ERRANT F0.5 or GLEU. CEFR-J study: grammar-error-rate ~0.73 correlation with human grammar-accuracy scores.
Yule's K (vocabulary repetitiveness) and Maas index a^2 = (log N - log V) / (log N)^2 — alternative length-robust richness measures available in lexicalrichness.
recommendations: Make the verbatim engine a hard dependency upstream of all filler/pause/repetition metrics. Standard Whisper output will silently under-report fillers and make any filler-rate score wrong; gate the pipeline on CrisperWhisper / whisper-timestamped (or a transcript-free Praat path) before computing those metrics.

Compute timing metrics from AUDIO, not from the transcript word count alone. WPM-from-transcript ignores pauses; add the parselmouth/Praat path (my-voice-analysis / de Jong-Wempe) to get true speech rate, articulation rate, and phonation-time ratio — these three together diagnose 'too fast' vs 'too many pauses,' which WPM alone cannot.

Replace raw TTR as the vocabulary-richness score. Swap in MATTR (window=50) or MTLD via the lexicalrichness package; keep TTR only for fixed-length comparisons. This is a correctness fix to the already-found tools that score TTR directly across variable-length responses.

Treat WPM 'ideal' as a configurable band, defaulting to 130-160 WPM (or 120-160 Toastmasters), not a hardcoded 111-140; expose presentation-type presets (technical 130-140, persuasive 150-160). Cite the band's source in the rubric so it is defensible.

Do not penalize normal-for-speech traits: lexical density below 40% and a small number of filled pauses (~2/100 words) are baseline for fluent spontaneous speech. Set elevated-filler flags at >~6/100 and distracting at >~10/100, anchored to Bortfeld et al. 2001, rather than 'zero fillers = perfect.'

Adopt a construct-driven composite (the SpeechRater model): score fluency, pronunciation, prosody, vocabulary, grammar, and content as separate sub-scores with documented thresholds, then weight — this is more defensible, more actionable for learners, and aligns the hobbyist tools with the research standard (Zechner/Loukina; ~24 features in SpeechRater v5).

For grammar, pair a GEC corrector with ERRANT to get errors-per-100-words AND a per-error-type breakdown; report types (article, agreement, tense) for actionable feedback rather than a single grammar number.

Apply Flesch-Kincaid to transcripts for relative tracking (improvement over sessions), not as an absolute verdict — readability formulas were validated on written prose and over-penalize the short clauses typical of good spoken delivery.

angle: Detecting weak/vague/hedging/filler words and overused intensifiers, suggesting stronger replacements (synonym strength + LLM rewrite), and detecting word-finding difficulty by fusing word-choice flags with timestamp/pause signals — i.e., the lexicon + linter + LLM-as-judge layer that sits on top of a verbatim-ASR filler counter. KEY CONSTRAINT (preserved and correct): mainstream ASR (Whisper, Google STT) silently deletes fillers and disfluencies, so a verbatim engine (CrisperWhisper, whisper-timestamped with word timestamps, faster-whisper with a verbatim/disfluency prompt) is mandatory upstream; everything in this angle consumes that verbatim, word-timestamped transcript. The pipeline is three stages: (1) FLAG weak/hedge/filler/intensifier words via curated lexicons + rule linters; (2) SUGGEST a stronger word via synonym-strength scoring (word norms / WordNet / thesaurus) or LLM rewrite; (3) DETECT 'got tripped up' moments by intersecting lexical hedge/vagueness flags with acoustic pause + disfluency features from the timestamps (a hedge word right after a long silent pause = high-confidence word-finding event).

repos.techniques: Per-word timestamps + confidence; derive inter-word gaps (silent pauses), low-confidence tokens, and filled-pause tokens as 'tripped up' features

techniques: LEXICON LAYER (flag): maintain four merged word/phrase lists — (a) FILLERS (um, uh, er, ah, like, you know, I mean, so, well, basically, actually, literally, right, okay, kinda, sort of); (b) HEDGES/qualifiers (maybe, perhaps, possibly, kind of, I guess, I think, sort of, somewhat, probably, might, could, seems, apparently); (c) WEASEL words (many, some, various, several, fairly, quite, surprisingly); (d) INTENSIFIERS/boosters (very, really, extremely, totally, absolutely, super, definitely). Source them from write-good (lib/weasel-words, lib/adverb), retext-intensify, proselint weasel_words+hedging checks, and LIWC tentative/certainty categories.

RULE-LINTER LAYER (flag, fast, deterministic): run proselint (weasel_words, hedging, redundancy, lexical_illusions, hyperbole) and write-good / the retext pipeline (retext-intensify + retext-passive + retext-simplify + retext-repeated-words) and capture each flag's character offsets so they can be aligned back to ASR word timestamps. These are CI-grade and need no model.

ML HEDGE LAYER (flag, context-aware): for context-dependent hedges a static list misses, run a BERT hedge/uncertainty token-classifier (BERTUncertaintyDetection) or fine-tune on CoNLL-2010/BioScope/HedgePeer cue annotations. Use this to catch 'that might work' vs 'might' as a noun.

SYNONYM-STRENGTH LAYER (suggest): for each flagged weak word, expand candidates via WordNet synsets + a thesaurus (PyDictionary/Wordnik), then RANK candidates by psycholinguistic norms — prefer higher concreteness (Brysbaert), lower corpus frequency / more specific (SUBTLEX), appropriate POS — to surface a genuinely stronger word rather than a random synonym. retext-simplify and LanguageTool provide ready phrase->replacement dictionaries for the common cases.

LLM-AS-JUDGE LAYER (suggest + score): use a calibrated rubric (LLM-Rubric pattern) scoring dimensions like word precision, confidence/assertiveness, conciseness, and filler density; pair with an automatic post-editor (Rubric-MQM pattern) that returns a stronger rewrite + rationale per span. Harden the judge prompt with Evidently's optimizer against human labels. Four-part judge prompt: criterion in domain words + forced step-by-step reasoning + deterministic score mapping + edge-case clause.

FUSION LAYER (detect 'got tripped up'): from the verbatim word-timestamped transcript compute per-word features — preceding silent-pause duration (gap to prior word end), filled-pause token present, ASR word confidence, local speech-rate dip, and self-repair/repetition span (joint disfluency parser). A word-finding / tripped-up event = a HEDGE or VAGUE-word flag OR low word-confidence co-located with an above-threshold silent pause and/or a filled pause and/or a repair. Score each candidate moment and rank.

CALIBRATION/THRESHOLDS: silent-pause threshold typically 250-500ms above the speaker's own median inter-word gap (per-speaker normalization beats a global constant); filler RATE = fillers / total words * 100; vocabulary richness via TTR / MTLD; benchmark word-finding flags against held-out human-annotated stumbles to set per-feature weights.

PRESERVED CONSTRAINT: do all of the above on a VERBATIM, word-timestamped transcript. Standard Whisper/Google STT strip fillers and smooth disfluencies, which destroys both the filler counts and the pause/repair signals the fusion layer needs — so CrisperWhisper / whisper-timestamped / faster-whisper-with-verbatim-prompt is non-optional upstream.
metricsOrFormulas: Filler rate = (filler_count / total_words) * 100  (per SharathKumar787 rubric; report as fillers per 100 words)
Hedge density = hedge_word_count / total_words ; Booster/intensifier density = intensifier_count / total_words
Silent pause (per word i) = start_time[i] - end_time[i-1]; flag if > speaker_median_gap + k (k ~ 250-500ms) — per-speaker normalization
Word-finding event score = w1*hedge_flag + w2*vague_flag + w3*(pause_norm) + w4*(1 - asr_word_confidence) + w5*filled_pause + w6*repair_span ; rank moments by score
Type-Token Ratio (TTR) = unique_words / total_words ; prefer MTLD or MATTR for length-robust vocabulary richness
Concreteness gain of a replacement = concreteness(candidate) - concreteness(original)  (Brysbaert 1-5 scale); specificity gain ~ -log(freq_SUBTLEX)
Speech rate / WPM = words / minutes (rubric ideal band ~111-140 WPM); detect local rate dips around a candidate stumble vs rolling baseline
Readability consensus grade (retext-readability): flag a span if >=N of {Dale-Chall, Flesch-Kincaid, SMOG, Gunning-fog, ARI, Coleman-Liau, spache} exceed target grade
LLM-judge calibration: report judge-vs-human agreement (Spearman / quadratic-weighted kappa) before trusting scores (LLM-Rubric calibrates the answer distribution)
recommendations: Build the FLAG stage as a deterministic ensemble first: proselint (weasel_words+hedging+redundancy+lexical_illusions+hyperbole) + the retext pipeline (retext-intensify + retext-passive + retext-simplify + retext-repeated-words) + write-good. All are permissive (BSD-3 / MIT) and emit character offsets — no model, CI-friendly, and the union of their word lists is a free filler/hedge/intensifier lexicon. (Correction to the brief: proselint is BSD-3-Clause and is primarily a Python package; write-good and the retext family are MIT JS.)

Merge a single canonical lexicon from write-good (lib/weasel-words, lib/adverb), retext-intensify's weak/mitigating list, proselint's weasel+hedging lists, LIWC tentative/certainty categories, and the CoNLL-2010/BioScope/HedgePeer hedge-cue sets — dedupe and tag each entry as filler|hedge|weasel|intensifier so downstream scoring can weight them differently.

Make the verbatim word-timestamped transcript the hard upstream dependency (CrisperWhisper for verbatim fillers; whisper-timestamped for per-word times+confidence). Note the license trap: CrisperWhisper is CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial) and whisper-timestamped is AGPL-3.0 — if the product is commercial, use faster-whisper with a verbatim/disfluency prompt or WhisperX word alignment instead.

For the SUGGEST stage, do NOT hand back raw WordNet synonyms — rank candidates by Brysbaert concreteness + SUBTLEX frequency so the replacement is measurably stronger/more specific; reserve the LLM rewrite (Rubric-MQM-style post-editor) for phrase-level fixes where a single-word swap won't carry the meaning.

Use LLM-as-judge only as the top calibrated layer, not the flag layer: prompt per dimension (precision, confidence, filler density, conciseness) with the LLM-Rubric pattern, calibrate against a small human-labeled set, and harden the prompt with Evidently's optimizer. Always report judge-vs-human agreement so scores are trustworthy.

Implement the 'got tripped up' detector as the FUSION of lexical + acoustic signals, never lexical alone: a hedge/vague word is only a confident word-finding event when co-located with an above-baseline SILENT pause, a filled pause, low ASR word-confidence, or a self-repair span from a disfluency parser (pariajm joint detector). Normalize pause thresholds per speaker.

Validate end-to-end against a small human-annotated set of real stumbles to learn the fusion weights (w1..w6) and pause threshold k — the brief's existing feedback systems (unruli, SpeakEZ, AI-Transcript-Scoring-Tool) are good integration references but they score globally; the differentiator here is per-MOMENT, timestamp-anchored word-finding detection.

Mind licenses for a shippable product: proselint BSD-3, write-good/retext/alex/empath MIT, Evidently Apache-2.0, LLM-Rubric MIT are all clean; LanguageTool is LGPL-2.1 (linkable but self-host the server); GPL/AGPL/CC-BY-NC components (unruli GPL-3.0, whisper-timestamped AGPL-3.0, CrisperWhisper CC-BY-NC) need isolation or replacement; treat undeclared research repos (BERTUncertaintyDetection, Rubric-MQM, HedgePeer) as verify-before-use.

angle: Open-source acoustic/prosody analysis libraries that power delivery-quality metrics (monotone, too-fast/too-slow, long-awkward-pauses, low-energy/flat) from the audio signal itself. These complement, rather than replace, the verbatim-ASR layer: ASR gives words, fillers, and word-level timestamps; the prosody layer turns the waveform into pitch (F0), energy/loudness, rate, and pause structure. The six requested libraries split into three tiers: (1) raw signal toolkits you compose yourself (Librosa, Parselmouth/Praat, pyAudioAnalysis) — maximum control, you write the metric formulas; (2) clinical/feature-set extractors that hand you named prosody features (DisVoice, openSMILE eGeMAPS) — research-validated descriptors; (3) turnkey but stale wrappers (my-voice-analysis, myprosody) — they output exactly the delivery metrics you want (rate of speech, articulation rate, pauses, balance ratio, F0 stats) with one call, but are unmaintained Praat-script wrappers with packaging/Python-3 breakage. CRITICAL preserved insight: standard ASR (Whisper/Google) deliberately strips fillers, so a verbatim engine (CrisperWhisper, whisper-timestamped) is mandatory to COUNT fillers — but the prosody layer here measures HOW words are delivered and does not need transcription at all, so the two layers are orthogonal and should run in parallel on the same audio.

repos.name: Parselmouth (praat-parselmouth)
repos.whatItDoes: Pythonic bindings to Praat's actual C/C++ internals (not a script wrapper). The gold standard for F0/pitch, intensity/loudness, formants, harmonicity (HNR), jitter/shimmer (via PointProcess), and voiced/unvoiced detection. Powers monotone detection (F0 std/range/CV over voiced frames), loudness dynamics (intensity contour std/range), and is the engine under my-voice-analysis, myprosody, and DisVoice's prosody module.
repos.libraries: pybind11, numpy; pip install praat-parselmouth (import parselmouth). Pairs with librosa for I/O.
repos.license: GPL-3.0-or-later (Praat itself is GPL) — copyleft, matters for distribution
repos.techniques: snd=parselmouth.Sound(wav); pitch=snd.to_pitch(); f0=pitch.selected_array['frequency']; f0=f0[f0>0] (drop unvoiced); monotone=np.std(f0) or np.std(f0)/np.mean(f0) (CV); intensity=snd.to_intensity(); energy_dynamics=np.std(intensity.values). PointProcess + to_harmonicity() give jitter/shimmer/HNR for voice quality.

repos.name: Librosa
repos.whatItDoes: General-purpose audio analysis. For delivery quality it provides RMS energy (loudness dynamics), pitch via pyin (probabilistic YIN, returns f0 + voiced_flag + voiced_probs — directly usable for voiced/unvoiced ratio and monotone), onset/tempo, zero-crossing rate, and MFCC/spectral features. Also the de-facto loader (librosa.load resamples to a target SR). Best for energy/pause-via-silence and as the feature backbone in Whisper+Librosa feedback systems (e.g. unruli/Real-Time-Feedback-System).
repos.libraries: numpy, scipy, soundfile, numba; pip install librosa
repos.techniques: f0,voiced_flag,voiced_prob=librosa.pyin(y,fmin=65,fmax=300,sr=sr); vu_ratio=voiced_flag.mean(); monotone=np.nanstd(f0[voiced_flag]). rms=librosa.feature.rms(y=y)[0]; energy_dynamics=rms.std()/rms.mean(). Pauses: intervals=librosa.effects.split(y,top_db=30); gaps between intervals = pauses; long_pause=gap>0.7s. WPM/articulation rate needs word timestamps from the ASR layer.

repos.name: openSMILE (opensmile-python)
repos.whatItDoes: Industrial feature extractor. Hands you the standardized eGeMAPS/GeMAPS and ComParE_2016 sets as a single pandas DataFrame. eGeMAPSv02 = 88 functionals built from LLDs incl. F0 (mean/percentiles/std/range — monotone), loudness (mean/std/range/rise — energy dynamics), jitter, shimmer, HNR, spectral flux, plus voiced/unvoiced segment lengths and rate-related stats. The fastest way to get research-validated, paper-citable delivery features without writing formulas.
repos.libraries: audonnx-free C backend wrapped in python; pip install opensmile (numpy/pandas/audeer)
repos.license: CORRECTION to common assumption: NOT plain open-source for all uses. Dual-licensed — free for private/research/educational use only; commercial use requires a paid audEERING license. Flag this for any shipped/commercial product.
repos.techniques: smile=opensmile.Smile(feature_set=opensmile.FeatureSet.eGeMAPSv02, feature_level=opensmile.FeatureLevel.Functionals); df=smile.process_file(wav). Read F0semitoneFrom27.5Hz_sma3nz_stddevNorm (monotone), loudness_sma3_stddevNorm (energy dynamics), MeanVoicedSegmentLengthSec / MeanUnvoicedSegmentLengthSec (pace+pause proxies), VoicedSegmentsPerSec (articulation proxy).

repos.name: DisVoice
repos.whatItDoes: Clinical speech-feature toolkit (built for dysarthria/Parkinson research) with a dedicated Prosody module computing F0 statistics (mean/std/max/min/skewness/kurtosis on contour, slopes), energy/intensity contour statistics, and duration features: voiced-segment durations, unvoiced/pause durations, and their distributions — i.e. exactly the pace, pause-distribution, and monotone primitives. Other modules: phonation (jitter/shimmer/APQ/PPQ), articulation, glottal, phonological. Returns static (one vector/file) or dynamic (per-frame) features.
repos.libraries: praat-parselmouth, kaldi-io, scipy, scikit-learn, pysptk, torch; install from repo (pip install disvoice / git clone)
repos.license: MIT (permissive — safe for commercial, unlike openSMILE)
repos.techniques: from disvoice.prosody import Prosody; p=Prosody(); feats=p.extract_features_file(wav, static=True, plots=False, fmt='dataframe'). Static vector exposes F0 avg/std (monotone), max/min F0, voiced-rate, and avg/std of voiced + unvoiced (pause) segment durations — pause distribution comes straight out. Permissive license makes it the best 'named features + shippable' option.

repos.name: pyAudioAnalysis
repos.whatItDoes: Broad audio-ML toolkit. For delivery quality its most useful pieces are silence_removal (energy+SVM-based VAD that segments speech vs silence — gives you pause segments and their durations/distribution directly) and short-term feature extraction (energy, energy entropy, ZCR, spectral, MFCC, chroma — 34 features). Also classification, segmentation, and speaker diarization. Good for pause distribution and energy dynamics; weaker for precise F0 than Parselmouth.
repos.libraries: numpy, scipy, scikit-learn, hmmlearn, eyed3, pydub; pip install pyAudioAnalysis
repos.techniques: from pyAudioAnalysis.audioSegmentation import silence_removal; segs=silence_removal(x,Fs,0.05,0.05,smoothWindow=1.0,weight=0.3) -> list of [start,end] speech regions; complements (gaps) = pauses -> count long pauses, pause-rate, pause-duration histogram. ShortTermFeatures.feature_extraction gives per-frame energy for loudness-dynamics std/range.

repos.name: my-voice-analysis
repos.whatItDoes: Turnkey Praat-script wrapper that, from a raw wav, outputs the delivery metrics almost verbatim: number of syllables, number of pauses, rate of speech (syll/sec over total), articulation rate (syll/sec over speaking time only), speaking duration (excl. pauses), total duration, balance ratio (speaking/total — a flow/pause-heaviness index), and F0 mean/std/median/min/max/q25/q75. Detects syllable nuclei acoustically, so NO transcript needed for pace/pause/monotone. Directly powers 'too fast' (rate of speech), 'monotone' (F0 std), 'long awkward pauses' (n_pauses + low balance ratio).
repos.libraries: Wraps Praat via the bundled myspsolution.praat script; needs numpy, scipy, pandas. Requires 44.1kHz/16-bit mono wav.
repos.techniques: import myspsolution as mysp; mysp.myspsr(name,path) (rate of speech), mysp.myspatc (articulation rate), mysp.myspst (speaking time), mysp.mysppaus (pauses), mysp.myspbala (balance), mysp.myspf0sd (F0 std=monotone). CAVEAT: unmaintained (~2019), pip packaging broken, Python-3.7-era; many users vendor the .praat script and call it via Parselmouth instead. Treat as a reference recipe more than a dependency.

repos.name: myprosody
repos.whatItDoes: Sister project to my-voice-analysis, extended for non-native/native comparison and CEFR/TOEFL-style scoring. Adds average syllable pause duration, count of long pauses, intonation index, F2/F1 ratio (formant-based vowel-space), Shannon entropy, gender/mood, and a proficiency estimate on top of the same rate/articulation/pause/F0 stack. Useful as a formula reference for 'long awkward pauses' (avg pause duration + long-pause count) and intonation/monotone scoring.
repos.libraries: Praat script + numpy, scipy, pandas, scikit-learn, hmmlearn (ships pre-trained model files).
repos.techniques: import myprosody as mysp; mysp.mysptotal(...) returns the full feature table incl. avg syllable pause duration and n long pauses (direct 'awkward pause' signals) plus intonation index (monotone). SAME maintenance caveat as my-voice-analysis — broken packaging, dated; mine it for the metric definitions and reimplement on Parselmouth for production.

repos.name: ProPer_Projekt
repos.whatItDoes: BONUS / breadth: an R+Praat academic workflow built specifically around continuous periodic-energy and F0 measurement — pitch contours, prominence, speech-rate, syllabic structure, with rich visualizations and quantification. Strong reference for principled monotone/prominence quantification (it weights F0 by periodic energy so unreliable pitch in low-energy frames is down-weighted — a refinement over naive F0-std monotone metrics).
repos.libraries: R + RStudio + Praat (not a Python library)
repos.license: GPL-3.0 (typical for Praat-derived workflows; verify in repo)
repos.techniques: Methodology to borrow: weight F0 variance by periodic-energy mass before computing monotone score, so silences/breathy frames don't pollute the pitch-range metric. Reimplementable in Parselmouth (intensity-weighted F0 std).

techniques: Monotone (pitch variance): extract F0 with Parselmouth to_pitch() or librosa.pyin, keep only voiced frames (f0>0), then monotone_score = std(f0) in semitones, or coefficient of variation std/mean, or F0 range (p95-p5). Convert Hz->semitones (12*log2(f0/ref)) before std so the metric is perception-aligned and speaker-pitch-independent. eGeMAPS field F0semitoneFrom27.5Hz_..._stddevNorm is the validated turnkey version.

Refined monotone: weight F0 by frame periodic energy / intensity before taking variance (ProPer approach) so low-energy/breathy frames with unreliable pitch don't distort the range. In Parselmouth: align to_intensity() to to_pitch() frames, compute intensity-weighted F0 std.

Pace / 'too fast': two distinct rates — Speech Rate = total syllables / total duration (includes pauses); Articulation Rate = syllables / speaking duration (excludes pauses). A fast articulation rate with low balance ratio = rushed. Syllable nuclei can be detected acoustically (de Jong & Wempe Praat script, used by my-voice-analysis) without a transcript; or use ASR word timestamps for WPM.

WPM from ASR layer: WPM = (word_count / speech_duration_sec) * 60. Ideal band ~111-150 WPM (the AI-Transcript-Scoring-Tool used 111-140; public-speaking norms ~130-150). Flag too_fast > ~160-170, too_slow < ~110. Needs word timestamps from the VERBATIM ASR layer (CrisperWhisper / whisper-timestamped), not the prosody layer.

Pause detection (two methods): (a) energy-VAD — librosa.effects.split(top_db=30) or pyAudioAnalysis silence_removal; gaps between speech segments are pauses. (b) ASR inter-word gaps — time between consecutive word end/start from whisper-timestamped. Method (b) distinguishes mid-sentence hesitation pauses from natural sentence-boundary pauses; method (a) needs no transcript.

Pause distribution / 'long awkward pauses': classify each pause: micro (<0.2s, ignore), normal (0.2-0.7s), long/awkward (>0.7-1.0s). Report long_pause_count, long_pause_rate (per minute), max_pause, and pause_duration histogram. Awkward-pause flag = long pauses occurring mid-clause (not at punctuation) — requires aligning pause timestamps to ASR token positions.

Loudness / energy dynamics: RMS energy contour (librosa.feature.rms) or Parselmouth to_intensity(). Flatness metric = std(intensity)/mean(intensity); very low = flat/under-projected delivery; report range (p95-p5 dB). eGeMAPS loudness_sma3_stddevNorm is the validated equivalent. Combine low energy-dynamics + low F0-variance => 'flat/monotone delivery' composite flag.

Articulation rate (signal-only): syllable_count (acoustic nuclei) / phonation_time (sum of voiced+short-pause speaking segments). my-voice-analysis myspatc and DisVoice voiced-segment stats both expose this without transcription.

Voiced/unvoiced ratio: from librosa.pyin voiced_flag.mean(), or DisVoice voiced/unvoiced segment durations, or Parselmouth pitch frames with f0>0. Low voiced ratio can indicate excessive breathiness, whispering, or heavy pausing; combine with energy to disambiguate.

Voice-quality add-ons (jitter/shimmer/HNR): Parselmouth PointProcess + to_harmonicity, or DisVoice phonation module, or eGeMAPS jitterLocal/shimmerLocaldB/HNRdBACF. High jitter/shimmer or low HNR => shaky/strained voice — a secondary 'nervousness' signal beyond fillers.

Composite delivery scoring: z-score each metric (F0 CV, articulation rate, long-pause rate, energy dynamics) against a calibrated reference distribution, then map to labels. 'Monotone' = low F0-CV AND low energy-dynamics; 'too fast' = high articulation rate AND high WPM AND low balance ratio; 'awkward pauses' = high mid-clause long-pause rate. Calibrate thresholds on a labeled sample, don't hardcode raw values across mics/rooms.

ORTHOGONALITY (preserved insight): the prosody layer (this angle) measures HOW it's delivered from the waveform and needs NO transcript; the verbatim-ASR layer measures fillers/words and DOES need a verbatim engine (Whisper/Google strip fillers by design). Run both in parallel on the same wav, then fuse on a shared time axis (align pauses/energy to ASR word/token timestamps) for the richest feedback (e.g. 'long pause before filler', 'rushed during low-energy section').
metricsOrFormulas: Monotone score (Hz): std(f0_voiced); pitch_range = percentile(f0,95) - percentile(f0,5)
Monotone score (perceptual): f0_st = 12*log2(f0/ref_Hz); monotone = std(f0_st); lower std => more monotone
Pitch coefficient of variation: F0_CV = std(f0_voiced)/mean(f0_voiced) (speaker-independent)
Speech Rate = syllable_count / total_duration_sec (syll/sec)
Articulation Rate = syllable_count / phonation_time_sec (syll/sec, pauses excluded)
WPM = word_count / speech_duration_sec * 60 ; ideal ~111-150, too_fast > ~160-170, too_slow < ~110
Balance ratio = speaking_duration / total_duration (low => pause-heavy / halting)
Pause classes: micro <0.2s | normal 0.2-0.7s | long/awkward >0.7s ; long_pause_rate = long_pauses / minutes
Energy dynamics (loudness flatness) = std(RMS)/mean(RMS) ; energy_range = p95(dB)-p5(dB)
Voiced/unvoiced ratio = voiced_frames / total_frames (from pyin voiced_flag or f0>0)
Mean voiced segment length & mean unvoiced (pause) segment length (eGeMAPS / DisVoice) — pace + pause proxies
Filler rate = fillers / total_words * 100 (from VERBATIM ASR layer; preserved from AI-Transcript-Scoring-Tool)
Voice quality: jitter (local), shimmer (local dB), HNR (dB) — shaky/strained-voice signal
Composite flat-delivery flag = (F0_CV low) AND (energy_dynamics low) ; rushed flag = (articulation_rate high) AND (balance_ratio low)
recommendations: Build the prosody layer on Parselmouth + Librosa as the production core: Parselmouth for F0/intensity/HNR/jitter-shimmer (accurate, Praat-grade), Librosa for I/O, RMS energy, pyin voiced-flag, and pause-via-silence. Both are well-maintained; you write the metric formulas and own the thresholds. This is the highest-leverage, license-clean foundation.

Use my-voice-analysis and myprosody as FORMULA REFERENCES, not runtime dependencies. They output exactly your target metrics (rate of speech, articulation rate, pauses, balance ratio, F0 stats) but are unmaintained (~2019), Python-3.7-era, with broken pip packaging. Best practice (and what the community does): vendor the bundled de Jong & Wempe syllable-nuclei .praat script and call it through Parselmouth in your own code.

For research-validated named features fast, add DisVoice (prosody module) — MIT-licensed, so safe to ship — before reaching for openSMILE. DisVoice gives F0, energy, and voiced/unvoiced + pause segment-duration stats in one call.

WATCH THE LICENSE on openSMILE: it is dual-licensed, free ONLY for private/research/educational use; any commercial product needs a paid audEERING license. eGeMAPS is excellent and citable, but for a shipped product prefer DisVoice (MIT), pyAudioAnalysis (Apache-2.0), or roll-your-own on Parselmouth. Also note Parselmouth itself is GPL-3.0 (copyleft) — fine for internal/SaaS use, a consideration for distributed binaries.

Keep the two layers strictly separate and run in parallel: (1) VERBATIM ASR layer for fillers/words/timestamps — CrisperWhisper (CC BY-NC 4.0, non-commercial) or whisper-timestamped (more permissive) — because standard ASR strips fillers; (2) this acoustic prosody layer for monotone/pace/pauses/energy, which needs no transcript. Fuse them on a shared time axis afterward.

Fuse for the highest-value feedback: align pause and energy events to ASR word/token timestamps so you can say 'long pause + filler mid-sentence' or 'rushed during the low-energy closing' — far more actionable than per-metric scores. This pairing of energy-VAD pauses with ASR inter-word gaps is the single biggest accuracy win for 'awkward pause' detection.

Calibrate thresholds, don't hardcode. WPM bands, long-pause cutoffs, and especially energy dynamics drift with microphone, room, and speaker baseline. Z-score each metric against a small labeled reference set and map z-scores to labels (monotone/too-fast/awkward-pauses) rather than shipping raw constants.

For monotone specifically, upgrade the naive std(F0) metric two ways: (a) compute it in semitones (perceptual + speaker-pitch-independent), and (b) energy-weight the F0 variance (ProPer methodology) so breathy/low-energy frames with garbage pitch don't pollute the range. Both are a few lines on top of Parselmouth.

Pin a reproducible environment for the older wrappers if you must run them: numba/numpy version conflicts plague librosa+pyAudioAnalysis+my-voice-analysis together. Isolate the Praat-script tools in their own venv or, better, eliminate them by reimplementing on Parselmouth.

Validate the pace primitive both ways: acoustic syllable-nuclei rate (no transcript) vs ASR WPM. Large disagreement flags either ASR errors or unusual speech (heavy accent, lots of non-lexical sound). Reporting both gives a robustness check and lets the system degrade gracefully when one layer is weak.

angle: Maximal taxonomy of speech-grading dimensions BEYOND fillers + word choice, triangulated from (a) commercial coach feature lists (Yoodli, Poised, Speeko, Vocal Image, Orai, Toastmasters Pathways) and (b) verifiable open-source repos/libraries, with the open-source computation recipe and a value-vs-effort call for each. Organized into four families: ACOUSTIC/PROSODIC (audio-only), LINGUISTIC/CONTENT (transcript-only), PARALINGUISTIC/AFFECT (audio or audio+text), and VISUAL/MULTIMODAL (video). Confirms the brief's key insight: standard ASR strips fillers, so a verbatim engine is mandatory to count them AND to get the accurate word-timestamps every pacing/pause/rate metric below depends on. Note one correction to a brief reference: openSMILE/eGeMAPS is NOT freely usable in a commercial product (dual license) — use Parselmouth/librosa/Silero for a permissively-licensed stack.

repos.name: Parselmouth (praat-parselmouth)
repos.whatItDoes: Python bindings to Praat. The workhorse for prosody: pitch (F0 mean/range/SD = intonation/monotone), intensity (loudness/energy), jitter & shimmer & HNR (voice quality/vocal strain/breathiness), formants. Backbone of most open-source vocal-variety scoring.
repos.libraries: Python C++ binding over Praat; pip install praat-parselmouth; pairs with numpy
repos.techniques: Intonation/pitch-variation, loudness/energy dynamics, vocal variety, voice quality (jitter/shimmer/HNR), monotone detection

repos.name: drfeinberg/PraatScripts
repos.whatItDoes: Ready-made Jupyter notebooks (Measure Pitch/HNR/Jitter/Shimmer; syllable-nuclei script) that wrap Parselmouth into copy-paste functions for pitch, HNR, jitter, shimmer, and automatic syllable/speech-rate detection. Fastest path to a vocal-variety + speech-rate baseline.
repos.libraries: Parselmouth, numpy, pandas
repos.techniques: Speech rate via syllable nuclei, pitch SD (intonation), jitter/shimmer (vocal strain)

repos.name: Shahabks/my-voice-analysis
repos.whatItDoes: Transcription-free Python lib over Praat that directly outputs speech rate (myspsr, syllables/sec over total duration), articulation rate (myspatc, syllables/sec over phonation time only), number of pauses (myspaus), a speaking 'balance' (phonation-to-total ratio), and F0 statistics. Near drop-in for pacing + pause + rate dimensions.
repos.libraries: Parselmouth/Praat under the hood; pip install my-voice-analysis
repos.techniques: Speech rate vs articulation rate split, pause count, speaking/pause balance, F0 stats. Sibling repos: Shahabks/myprosody (native-vs-learner prosody) and Shahabks/Speechat (MIT)

repos.whatItDoes: Tiny, fast, CPU-only neural Voice Activity Detector.
