techniques: VERBATIM ASR IS A PREREQUISITE, NOT A DIMENSION: every pacing/pause/rate/repetition metric needs accurate WORD-LEVEL timestamps, and filler counting needs un-normalized output. Use CrisperWhisper / whisper-timestamped / WhisperX (forced alignment) as the front-end; standard Whisper/Google strip fillers AND smooth timing.

ACOUSTIC/PROSODIC FAMILY (audio-only, Parselmouth/librosa/Silero): (1) Pace/WPM and its consistency over time; (2) Articulation rate vs speech rate split (phonation-only speed reveals rushing inside fluent stretches); (3) Pause quality — count, duration, placement, strategic(>=250-300ms) vs hesitation pauses, phonation/silence ratio; (4) Intonation / pitch variation (F0 mean/range/SD) -> monotone detection; (5) Loudness/energy dynamics (RMS, SD of RMS) -> flat-energy = low engagement; (6) Volume consistency / trailing-off; (7) Voice quality: jitter, shimmer, HNR -> vocal strain, breathiness, shakiness/nervousness; (8) Vocal variety composite (Toastmasters tone+speed+volume) = pitch SD + rate variance + loudness SD.

LINGUISTIC/CONTENT FAMILY (transcript-only, NLP): (9) Sentence complexity / readability (textstat: Flesch, FK grade, Gunning Fog, SMOG); (10) Lexical diversity / vocabulary richness (MTLD, HD-D, TTR via LexicalRichness); (11) Repetition & redundancy (n-gram repeat rate, crutch-word reliance, consecutive-word echo) — distinct from fillers; (12) Jargon / difficult-word density (textstat difficult_words + domain wordlists); (13) Inclusive / sensitive language (alex, blocklint); (14) Sentiment/tone of content (VADER/transformer sentiment over the transcript); (15) Structure / discourse (intro-body-close detection via cue phrases 'first/however/in conclusion'; signposting density; opener & closer strength) — best done with an LLM rubric pass; (16) Hedging / qualifier density ('I think', 'kind of', 'maybe') -> confidence proxy from text; (17) Question handling (in Q&A/interview: directness, latency-to-answer via timestamps, on-topic relevance via embedding similarity to the question).

PARALINGUISTIC / AFFECT FAMILY (audio or audio+text): (18) Emotion recognition (emotion2vec / wav2vec2-SER, 4-9 classes); (19) Tone/sentiment fusion (acoustic affect + text sentiment); (20) Confidence estimation (low jitter/shimmer + steady energy + few hedges + few hesitation pauses -> composite confidence score); (21) Energy / charisma / engagement (loudness dynamics + pitch variability + rate variability + spectral flux; POM-style persuasiveness models); (22) Stress/nervousness (shimmer + F0 instability + faster-than-baseline rate + filler-of-silence spikes); (23) Enthusiasm/warmth (smiling-AU + rising intonation + positive sentiment).

VISUAL / MULTIMODAL FAMILY (video, opt-in tier): (24) Eye contact / gaze toward camera (L2CS-Net preferred for license; OpenFace); (25) Facial expressiveness / smiling / animation (OpenFace AUs, MediaPipe face mesh); (26) Hand-gesture frequency & amplitude (MediaPipe Hands); (27) Posture / openness / leaning (MediaPipe Pose); (28) Head & body stability — sway/fidget/nervous-movement detection; (29) Slide/visual-aid quality (separate CV/heuristic pass).

PROGRESS / META DIMENSIONS (cut across all above): (30) Progress-over-time trend lines per metric (Poised/Yoodli core selling point) — store every session's scores, show deltas, rolling baselines, and personal targets; (31) Per-speaker normalization / personal baseline (compare to the user's own history, not just population norms) to avoid penalizing naturally deep/quiet voices; (32) Composite 'overall score' (Poised Score / Speeko 6-metric radar) = weighted blend, surfaced as a radar/spider chart.

LICENSING TRAPS to flag for a shippable product: openSMILE/eGeMAPS = dual license, NOT free for commercial products; OpenFace = academic/non-commercial only; CrisperWhisper = CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial); many feedback-system repos are GPL-3.0 (copyleft). Permissive (MIT/BSD/Apache) safe stack for commercial: Parselmouth is GPL so swap to librosa(ISC)+Silero-VAD(MIT)+whisper-timestamped/WhisperX(BSD/MIT)+emotion2vec(MIT)+L2CS-Net(MIT)+MediaPipe(Apache)+textstat(MIT)+LexicalRichness(MIT)+alex(MIT).
metricsOrFormulas: WPM = (total words / total speaking minutes); commonly cited ideal conversational/presentation band ~ 110-150 wpm (brief's SharathKumar tool uses 111-140). Compute over rolling windows to get pace CONSISTENCY = SD of windowed WPM (lower = steadier).

Articulation rate = syllables / phonation-time-only (excludes pauses); Speech rate = syllables / total time. Articulation >> speech rate means many/long pauses. Both via my-voice-analysis (myspatc/myspsr) or syllable-nuclei script.

Pause analysis from VAD: silence_ratio = total_silence / total_duration; classify gaps: <250ms = micro/hesitation, 250ms-1s = rhetorical/strategic, >1.5-2s = dead air. Score = reward strategic pauses, penalize dead air and high hesitation-gap count.
Filler rate = (filler_count / total_words) * 100 (brief's rubric). Requires verbatim ASR. Extend filler list with timestamps to map filler density over the timeline.
Intonation/monotone: F0 in semitones; pitch_variation = SD(F0_semitones) or pitch range (P95-P5). Low SD over a long window = monotone flag. eGeMAPS uses F0 semitone mean/SD.

Energy dynamics: frame RMS (librosa.feature.rms) or eGeMAPS loudness; flat_energy_flag when SD(RMS) below a personal/population threshold (research: flatter vocal dynamics correlate with poorer perceived engagement).
Voice quality: local jitter (cycle-to-cycle F0 perturbation), local shimmer (amplitude perturbation), HNR (Parselmouth). Elevated jitter/shimmer + lower HNR -> strained/shaky/nervous voice.

Lexical diversity: TTR = unique_words/total_words (length-biased); prefer MTLD (segments text until TTR drops to 0.72, averages factor lengths) or HD-D (hypergeometric) — both length-robust. Higher = richer, less repetitive.

Readability: Flesch Reading Ease = 206.835 - 1.015*(words/sentences) - 84.6*(syllables/words); Flesch-Kincaid Grade = 0.39*(words/sentences) + 11.8*(syllables/words) - 15.59. Lower FK grade = more accessible spoken content.

Repetition/redundancy: repeated n-gram rate = count of bigrams/trigrams occurring > k times / total; immediate-repeat rate = adjacent duplicate tokens / total. Complements filler counting for 'crutch phrase' detection.

Hedging/confidence-from-text: hedge_density = hedge_phrase_hits / total_words against a lexicon ('I think','kind of','sort of','maybe','just','probably','I guess'). Lower hedging + steady prosody -> higher confidence sub-score.

Composite confidence (audio+text): z-score and weight-blend = w1*(-jitter) + w2*(-shimmer) + w3*(energy_SD_norm) + w4*(-hesitation_pause_rate) + w5*(-hedge_density) + w6*(-filler_rate). Calibrate weights to human ratings (e.g., POM-style labels).
Eye-contact %: frames with gaze_yaw,pitch within +/- threshold of camera direction / total frames (L2CS-Net or OpenFace gaze). Report % on-camera + longest look-away streak.
Gesture rate: detected distinct hand-gesture events / minute (MediaPipe Hands landmark motion peaks); pair with amplitude (bounding-box displacement) for 'expressive vs static'.

Overall/composite score (Speeko/Poised pattern): normalize each dimension to 0-100 vs personal+population baseline, then weighted average -> single score + radar chart; track session-over-session deltas for the progress dimension.
recommendations: Make a verbatim, word-timestamped ASR front-end the non-negotiable foundation: it is a prerequisite for fillers AND for pacing/pause/rate/repetition/question-latency. For a commercial product, pick a permissive engine (WhisperX or whisper-timestamped, BSD/MIT) and reserve CrisperWhisper (CC BY-NC) for research/eval benchmarking only.

Ship in value-vs-effort tiers. TIER 1 (highest value, lowest effort, audio+transcript only): pace/WPM + consistency, pause quality, filler rate, intonation/monotone (F0 SD), energy dynamics, readability/sentence-complexity, lexical diversity, repetition, hedging, inclusive language. All from Parselmouth/librosa + Silero-VAD + textstat + LexicalRichness + alex — a few hundred lines, no training, no GPU.

TIER 2 (high value, medium effort, pretrained models): speech emotion/tone (emotion2vec, MIT), pronunciation/enunciation scoring (GOPT + speechocean762), composite confidence and energy/charisma blends. Pretrained weights exist; mostly inference + calibration to human ratings.

TIER 3 (high perceived value, high effort + privacy/UX cost, video): eye contact (L2CS-Net), facial expressiveness (MediaPipe/OpenFace), gesture/posture (MediaPipe). Gate behind explicit opt-in and on-device processing; prefer MediaPipe(Apache)+L2CS-Net(MIT) over OpenFace to avoid the academic-only license.

Treat structure (intro/body/close, signposting, opener/closer strength) and question-handling as an LLM-rubric pass over the transcript rather than classical NLP — far less brittle than discourse-marker heuristics and lets you emit human-readable coaching, mirroring unruli's Whisper+Llama-3 blueprint.

Build progress-over-time and personal-baseline normalization in from day one — it is the retention engine for Poised and Yoodli, is nearly free once you persist per-session scores, and prevents unfair penalties for naturally deep/quiet/accented voices (normalize to the user's own history + offer population bands as context).

Correct the working assumption on openSMILE/eGeMAPS: it is source-available with a dual license and is NOT free for use inside a commercial product, and OpenFace is non-commercial too. Default to the permissive stack (librosa, Silero-VAD, emotion2vec, L2CS-Net, MediaPipe, textstat, LexicalRichness, alex) and only pull GPL/NC tools into research/eval paths.

Avoid double-counting and false precision: fillers, hesitation pauses, hedging, and repetition all proxy 'low confidence/fluency' — blend them into one fluency/confidence index rather than penalizing four times, and always show the timestamped evidence (the highlighted moment) next to every score so feedback is actionable, not just a number.
